title: EXERCISE: Hamlet of Ridgewater spring boreal fire (fictional community)
summary: A leaf-off spring fire north-west of a fictional boreal hamlet on a highway. A wind shift the forecast missed turns the fire back toward the highway.

caveats: Fictional community name on real geography (owner decision 2026-10-30): nothing here describes or predicts a real community.
The Alberta grid maps little vegetation inside towns and treats cropland as non-fuel (docs/fuel-grid-alberta.md).
Building footprints: Microsoft (2019 imagery) with uneven coverage; newer houses missing.
Weather and FWI codes are scripted exercise values, not observations or a forecast.
Multi-day runs hold one weather per 24 h day: the T+20 h wind shift reaches the model at T+24 h (day 2) unless a restart carries it earlier.

FireSim is a preparedness and training tool: held-out one-day skill is low (F1 0.246 on the pre-fire grid) and the ensemble is over-confident (49 % coverage). The fire in this pack is a scripted stimulus, not a prediction.

notesForFacilitator: EXERCISE. Facilitator only: the geography is the Wandering River area (Athabasca County, Highway 63); the pack calls the hamlet Ridgewater, a fictional name. Truth: SE 15 km/h, 22 °C, 25 % RH from 13:00 MDT on 5 May (leaf-off: D-1 / M-1 by date); at T+20 h (09:00 on 6 May) the wind shifts to NW 30 km/h with RH 20 %, hidden from the players' forecast until the wind-shift inject. Ignition about 6.2 km NW of the hamlet and 4.5 km west of Highway 63 in a mapped C-1 stand of the Alberta grid (chosen by rule, see the PR2 record). Spot fire at T+22 h 0.6 km east of Highway 63 in mapped D-1/M-1 fuel (delivered from PR3 as a union-perimeter restart). Perimeter inject at T+26 h from the truth run. Values set by the owner 2026-10-30; checked against station climatology in PR2 (see the PR).
